question: What Do WooCommerce's Different Order Statuses Actually Mean?
metaDescription: Pending, on-hold, processing, completed, cancelled, refunded, and failed each represent a distinct point in the payment and fulfillment lifecycle.
shortAnswer: WooCommerce's core statuses map to specific points in an order's payment and fulfillment lifecycle: Pending payment (order created, payment not yet attempted or confirmed), On hold (awaiting manual payment confirmation, like a bank transfer), Processing (payment received, awaiting fulfillment), Completed (fulfilled and done), Cancelled (deliberately voided), Refunded (money returned), and Failed (payment attempt didn't succeed). Understanding this progression helps make sense of automated emails, stock behavior, and reporting, all of which key off these specific statuses.

bodyHtml:
The Core Statuses Explained

Each status exists to answer a specific question about where an order stands, and several WooCommerce behaviors (stock reduction, which emails fire, whether an order counts toward sales reports) are directly tied to these specific transitions rather than being arbitrary labels.

What Each Status Means

  • Pending payment — the order exists, but payment hasn't been confirmed yet; this is the initial state before a gateway responds.
  • On hold — awaiting manual confirmation, most commonly used for offline payment methods like bank transfer or cheque, where the store needs to manually verify payment arrived.
  • Processing — payment has been received (this is the trigger point for stock reduction by default) and the order is awaiting fulfillment/shipment.
  • Completed — the order has been fully fulfilled; for many stores this is set manually when an item ships, though some automate it.
  • Cancelled — the order was deliberately voided, by the customer or the store, before fulfillment.
  • Refunded — the order's payment has been returned, whether fully or partially.
  • Failed — a payment attempt was made but didn't succeed, and no successful payment followed.

Why This Matters Practically

  1. Stock reduction is tied to specific status transitions, not the moment of purchase, which explains some timing questions covered elsewhere.
  2. Automated customer emails fire on specific status changes, so understanding the flow helps diagnose "why didn't my customer get an email" questions.
  3. Reporting and analytics typically count only Processing/Completed orders as genuine sales, excluding Pending, Failed, and Cancelled ones.
